verdicts.note: Attacked toward 2: making the levy permanent ends the six-year re-votes [S6] and is a larger long-run commitment. But the maximum rate stays $0.50 [S1][S2], the 2026 rate is already about $0.48 [S5], and the levy has been in place and renewed [S4][S7][S8]; a same-rate continuation maps to 1, as in the Douglas Hospital District 2 and Cemetery District 2 reviews. A yes vote still continues a tax a no vote would let lapse after 2030 collection [S4], so 0 is wrong. S1, S2, S4 and S5 exist and support the basis; the 2018 approval comes from S8, which is not cited.

Mostly matches the dossier: permanent levy up to $0.50 from 2027 collection [S1][S2]; EMS-only use [S1][S2][S6]; Bickleton area excluded [S9]; 60% in RCW 84.52.069 vs simple majority in the resolution [S2][S6]; $250 on $500,000 and the 2026 rate of about $0.48 raising $2.56 million [S5]; 2,417 responses and 1,400 square miles from 2024 [S4]; no statements for or against [S1][S3]; about 74% twice [S7][S8]; 15% referral petition [S6]. Two wording problems. (1) what_it_does says voters renewed 'the same levy' in 2018 and 2024: the dossier gives the 2024 rate ($0.50 or less) but not the 2018 rate, so say 'renewed the levy for six years in 2018 and 2024'. (2) pro_summary says 'trained paramedics and EMTs'; the explanatory statement as recorded says 'trained emergency medical personnel' [S1][S3]. Optional: con_summary could note that the resolution does not mention the referendum procedure the statute requires [S2][S6].
